original_interpretation: The CHIPS Act of 2022 provides US$50 billion to the Department of Commerce plus authority for up to US$75 billion in direct loans and loan guarantees.
evidence_found: "A division of the CHIPS and Science Act, the CHIPS Act provides $50 billion to the Department of Commerce to support semiconductor research, development, innovation, and manufacturing, along with authorization for up to $75 billion in direct loans and loan guarantees." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 1); p. 2 repeats "the CHIPS Act provides for up to $75 billion in loan authority."
notes: Checked against OIG text extracted from the PDF itself. Per OIG p. 4, CPO allocated up to $38.2bn direct funding and up to $75bn loans/guarantees to the Commercial Fabs NOFO.

original_interpretation: As of 31 January 2025 the CHIPS Program Office had awarded up to US$33.7 billion of direct funding (US$30.7 billion of incentive awards plus US$3.0 billion for the Secure Enclave) and up to US$5.5 billion of loans, out of US$39 billion appropriated.
evidence_found: "As of January 31, 2025, CPO has awarded up to approximately $33.7 billion of direct funding" (p. 3); Table 1: "Incentive awards $30,663 $5,500 Secure enclave $3,000 – Awards subtotal $33,663 $5,500 ... Total $39,000 $5,500" (p. 3). Newer: CRS R49031 note 29: "This additional award brought the total direct funding awarded by the CHIPS incentives program to date to $30.9 billion, alongside $5.5 billion in loans."
correction: Correct as of 2025-01-31, but superseded: after Micron's +$275m award on 12 June 2025 CHIPS incentive direct funding totalled about $30.9bn (plus $5.5bn loans), i.e. about $33.9bn including the $3.0bn Secure Enclave (CRS R49031, note 29; see also CLM-0981). The Intel award was converted to equity in Aug 2025 (CLM-0259).
notes: Figures verified exactly for the stated date; OIG p.1 also says CPO made 20 awards.

original_interpretation: As of 31 January 2025 US$4.584 billion of the US$39 billion CHIPS incentives appropriation was unawarded and US$753 million was allotted to administrative expenses.
evidence_found: Table 1: "Administrative expenses $753 – Unawarded $4,584 – Total $39,000 $5,500" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 3)
notes: Accurate for 2025-01-31. The unawarded balance has since fallen by at least the $275m Micron add-on (June 2025); no newer official unawarded figure found in the sources checked.

original_interpretation: TSMC's CHIPS commercial-fab funding agreement comprised up to US$6.565 billion of direct funding and US$5.0 billion of loans (US$11.565 billion total federal investment).
evidence_found: Table 2: "Taiwan Semiconductor $6,565 $5,000 $11,565" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 5); CRS R49031 Table A-1 still lists "TSMC Arizona ... November 15, 2024 ... 11,565" as of July 2026.

original_interpretation: Intel's CHIPS commercial-fab funding agreement was up to US$7.865 billion of direct funding with no loans, as of 31 January 2025.
notes: Accurate as of 2025-01-31 and still listed at 7,865 in CRS R49031 Table A-1, but in Aug 2025 the funding was converted into a 9.9% equity stake: $5.7bn of the fab award to be disbursed promptly with milestone obligations released, plus $3.2bn Secure Enclave, $8.9bn total (CRS R49031; CLM-0259). Do not present $7.865bn as a milestone-based grant after Aug 2025.

original_interpretation: Micron's CHIPS commercial-fab funding agreement was up to US$6.165 billion of direct funding with no loans, as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: Table 2: "Micron $6,165 $0 $6,165" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 5). Newer: CRS R49031 Table A-1 note a: "Award for Micron was increased by $275 million to $6.44 billion on June 12, 2025."
correction: Correct as of 2025-01-31; Micron's award was increased by $275m to $6.44bn on 12 June 2025 (CRS R49031 Table A-1 note a; see CLM-0268).

original_interpretation: Samsung's CHIPS commercial-fab funding agreement was up to US$4.745 billion of direct funding with no loans, as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: Table 2: "Samsung $4,745 $0 $4,745" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 5); CRS Table A-1 lists 4,745 as of July 2026.

original_interpretation: Texas Instruments' CHIPS funding agreement was up to US$1.610 billion of direct funding with no loans, as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: Table 2: "Texas Instruments $1,610 $0 $1,610" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 5)

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries' CHIPS funding agreement was up to US$1.587 billion of direct funding with no loans, as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: Table 2: "Global Foundries $1,587 $0 $1,587" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 5)

original_interpretation: SK hynix's CHIPS funding agreement comprised up to US$458 million of direct funding and US$500 million of loans; TSMC and SK hynix were the only awardees with CHIPS loans (US$5.5 billion combined) as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: Table 2: "SK hynix $458 $500 $958" ... "Total $30,663 $5,500 $36,163"; all other rows show "$0" loans except "Taiwan Semiconductor $6,565 $5,000" (OIG-25-021-I, pp. 5-6)

original_interpretation: Smaller CHIPS funding agreements as of 31 January 2025 (direct funding, US$ million) were: Amkor 407, GlobalWafers 406, Hemlock Semiconductor 325, Polar Semiconductor 123, Infinera 93, Entegris 77, Absolics 75, HP 53, BAE 36, Corning 32, Rocket Lab (SolAero) 24, Edwards Vacuum 18.
evidence_found: Table 2 (pp. 5-6): "Amkor Technology $407 ... GlobalWafers $406 ... Hemlock Semiconductor $325 ... Polar Semiconductor $123 ... Infinera $93 ... Entegris $77 ... Absolics $75 ... HP $53 ... BAE $36 ... Corning $32 ... Rocket Lab (SolAero) $24 ... Edwards Vacuum $18"
notes: All 12 values match; CRS R49031 Table A-1 has the same values.

original_interpretation: Of CHIPS Program Office awards as of 31 January 2025, leading-edge logic received US$18.1 billion, leading-edge memory US$6.1 billion, current-generation/mature-node US$3.209 billion, Secure Enclave US$3.0 billion, wafer/materials/equipment US$1.484 billion, advanced packaging US$1.478 billion and workforce development US$293 million.
evidence_found: Figure 3. Funding by Category (in millions): "Workforce Development – $293 Wafer Manufacturing, Semiconductor Materials and Equipment – $1,484 Advanced Packaging – $1,478 Secure Enclave – $3,000 Current Generation Mature Node – $3,209 Leading-Edge Memory – $6,100 Leading-Edge Logic – $18,100" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 7)
notes: Categories are OIG/CPO primary-project categories; they sum to about $33.66bn. Memory category predates the June 2025 Micron +$275m add-on.

original_interpretation: The CHIPS Program Office's 2030 objective for leading-edge logic was at least two large-scale US clusters of leading-edge fabs expected to produce roughly 20 percent of the world's leading-edge chips.
evidence_found: "Leading-Edge Logic: The United States will have at least two new large-scale clusters of leading-edge logic fabrication facilities. These clusters ... are expected to produce roughly 20 percent of the world's leading-edge semiconductor chips." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 3, among "four objectives to achieve by 2030")
notes: A program objective (target), not an outcome.

original_interpretation: A preliminary memorandum of terms (PMT) under the CHIPS incentives program is a nonbinding agreement outlining the amount and form of a potential award; as of 31 January 2025, 15 nonbinding PMTs totalled up to about US$1.9 billion in direct funding and US$350 million in loans.
evidence_found: "PMTs are nonbinding2 agreements that outline key terms for a potential CHIPS incentives award, including the amount and form of the award." (p. 4); "As of January 31, 2025, there are 15 nonbinding PMTs totaling up to approximately $1.9 billion in direct funding and $350 million in loans." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 8)

original_interpretation: No awards had been made under the CHIPS materials and manufacturing-equipment NOFO (projects under US$300 million; up to US$500 million reserved) as of 31 January 2025.
evidence_found: "capital investments of less than $300 million" ... "CPO reserved up to $500 million for direct funding for this NOFO." (p. 8); "As of January 31, 2025, no awards have been made, and no funds have been committed or expended." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 9)

original_interpretation: Congress allocated up to US$3.5 billion of the US$39 billion CHIPS incentives appropriation to the Secure Enclave, and Intel was awarded up to US$3 billion for it on 16 September 2024, executed by the Department of Defense.
evidence_found: "Congress allocated up to $3.5 billion of the $39 billion originally appropriated for the CHIPS Incentives Program to support the Secure Enclave." ... "On September 16, 2024, Intel Corporation was awarded up to $3 billion in direct funding for the Secure Enclave. The award will be executed by the Department of Defense per an agreement with the Department of Commerce." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 9)
notes: Intel later reported the Secure Enclave award as $3.2bn (CRS R49031, Aug 2025).

original_interpretation: Because of the Secure Enclave funding requirement and high demand, the CHIPS Program Office announced on 29 March 2024 that it would not issue a funding opportunity for semiconductor R&D facilities.
evidence_found: "Due to the Secure Enclave funding requirement and high demand for CHIPS incentive funding, CPO announced on March 29, 2024, that it will not proceed with a NOFO for the construction, modernization, or expansion of semiconductor research and development facilities in the United States." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 9)

original_interpretation: As of 31 January 2025 the CHIPS R&D Office had awarded almost US$8.3 billion: NSTC US$6.355 billion, NAPMP US$1.4 billion, CHIPS Manufacturing USA Institute US$285 million, metrology US$252 million, SBIR US$5 million; US$2.488 billion of the US$11 billion remained unawarded.
evidence_found: Table 4: "NSTC $6,355 NAPMP $1,400 CHIPS Manufacturing USA Institute $285 Metrology $252 Small Business Innovation Research $5 Award subtotal $8,297 Administrative expenses $215 Unawarded $2,488 Total $11,000" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 10)

original_interpretation: As of 31 January 2025 NIST had awarded approximately US$6.3 billion to Natcast, the nonprofit incorporated on 19 October 2023 to operate the National Semiconductor Technology Center, using other transaction agreements.
evidence_found: "Natcast, a nonprofit organization, was incorporated on October 19, 2023, to operate the NSTC." ... "During FY 2024, Natcast and its programs were funded by CHIPS Act appropriations using OTAs. As of January 31, 2025, NIST awarded approximately $6.3 billion to Natcast" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 11)
notes: As-of Jan 2025 only; later developments at Natcast were not checked here.

original_interpretation: On 16 January 2025 the CHIPS R&D Office awarded Natcast approximately US$1.1 billion to operate the National Advanced Packaging Piloting Facility.
evidence_found: "On January 16, 2025, CRDO awarded Natcast approximately $1.1 billion to operate the NAPPF." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 12)

original_interpretation: On 3 January 2025 Commerce awarded the Semiconductor Research Corporation Manufacturing Consortium Corporation US$285 million to establish and operate the CHIPS Manufacturing USA institute SMART USA (digital twins).
evidence_found: "On January 3, 2025, the Department announced it awarded the Semiconductor Research Corporation Manufacturing Consortium Corporation $285 million to establish and operate a Manufacturing USA institute known as SMART USA (Semiconductor Manufacturing and Advanced Research with Twins USA)." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 15)

original_interpretation: On 16 January 2025 Commerce announced three NAPMP materials and substrates awards of US$100 million each to Absolics, Applied Materials and Arizona State University.
evidence_found: "On January 16, 2025, the Department announced three awards totaling $300 million for advanced substrates and material research" and Table 5: "Absolics, Inc. $100 Applied Materials, Inc. $100 Arizona State University $100 Total $300" (OIG-25-021-I, p. 13)

original_interpretation: Commerce OIG describes the US Investment Accelerator, created 31 March 2025, as having assumed responsibility for the CHIPS Program Office and being intended to facilitate and accelerate investments above US$1 billion.
evidence_found: "On March 31, 2025, the President issued an executive order establishing the United States Investment Accelerator within the Department of Commerce. This new office assumed responsibility for CPO and is intended to facilitate and accelerate investments above $1 billion." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 1)

original_interpretation: CHIPS award agreements move from nonbinding PMT through due diligence to a final award, after which funds are disbursed as the awardee meets project milestones.
evidence_found: "Full Application: ... the Department prepares a preliminary memorandum of terms (PMT). PMTs are nonbinding ..." "Due Diligence ..." "Award: During the award phase, CPO negotiates the final award documents with applicants ... Funding is expected to be disbursed as milestones are met." (OIG-25-021-I, p. 4)
notes: Applies to the Commercial Fabrication Facilities NOFO; Intel's Aug 2025 equity deal released it from milestone obligations (CLM-0935).

original_interpretation: CRS R49031 (July 2026) lists 19 companies with final CHIPS commercial-fab awards and reports 'total incentives' as the sum of direct funding and loans offered by Commerce.
evidence_found: "Table A-1. Companies with Final Awards from the Semiconductor Incentives Program for Commercial Fabs" (19 rows, Absolics to TSMC Arizona); note: "The total incentives in this table reflect the sum of both direct funding and loans offered by DOC." (CRS R49031, Appendix)
notes: Counted 19 company rows. Table source: NIST CHIPS for America Awards page accessed 7 July 2026.

original_interpretation: Final CHIPS award agreements for the largest recipients were announced in late 2024: TSMC 15 Nov 2024, GlobalFoundries 20 Nov 2024, Intel 26 Nov 2024, Micron 10 Dec 2024, SK hynix 19 Dec 2024, Samsung 20 Dec 2024 and Texas Instruments 20 Dec 2024.
evidence_found: CRS R49031 Table A-1 "Date of Final Award Announcement": "TSMC Arizona ... November 15, 2024"; "GlobalFoundries ... November 20, 2024"; "Intel Corporation ... November 26, 2024"; "Micron ... December 10, 2024"; "SK hynix ... December 19, 2024"; "Samsung ... December 20, 2024"; "Texas Instruments ... December 20, 2024"

original_interpretation: As of 10 June 2026, 12 companies held CHIPS preliminary memoranda of terms without final awards, including Wolfspeed (US$750 million proposed), Bosch (US$225 million), Microchip Technology (US$162 million) and Analog Devices (US$105 million).
evidence_found: Table A-2 "... without a Final Award as of June 10, 2026": "Wolfspeed | October 15, 2024 | 750"; "Bosch | December 13, 2024 | 225"; "Microchip Technology, Inc. | January 4, 2024 | 162"; "Analog Devices Inc. | January 16, 2025 | 105" (CRS R49031, Appendix); summary: "12 companies signed preliminary agreements ... As of June 2026, public records do not indicate whether these 12 companies have received final awards."
notes: Amounts are 'total incentives' (direct funding plus loans, up to). CRS wording is that public records do not indicate final awards, not that none exist.

original_interpretation: As of July 2026 CRS had not identified any CHIPS incentive award that had been publicly rescinded or reduced.
evidence_found: "As of July 2026, CRS has not identified any awards that have been publicly rescinded or reduced." (CRS R49031, Considerations for Congress / Award Requirements)
notes: Attributed statement of CRS's search. The same report notes Micron's award was increased and Intel's converted to equity; neither counts as rescinded or reduced in CRS's framing.

original_interpretation: Under the August 2025 equity arrangement, Intel stated it would be released from the project milestone obligations in its original CHIPS award contract, and the government would disburse US$5.7 billion as promptly as practicable.
evidence_found: "In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in August 2025, Intel elaborated that the government would disburse $5.7 billion 'as promptly as practicable' from the direct funding award for commercial semiconductor fabs. The SEC document noted that the company would be released from obligations to meet project milestones established in the original award contract." (CRS R49031, text box on Intel)
notes: Secondary (CRS) summary of Intel's Aug 2025 8-K; primary filing not re-opened here.

original_interpretation: The Intel-US government agreement permits the government to take an additional 5% stake in Intel at US$20 per share if Intel ceases to own 51% of its foundry business.
evidence_found: "The agreement between Intel and the U.S. government permits the government to take an additional 5% stake in Intel at $20 a share if the company were to cease to own 51% of its chip manufacturing (foundry) business." (CRS R49031, text box on Intel)
notes: CRS summary; the underlying agreement terms (e.g., warrant duration) were not checked in the primary filing.

original_interpretation: Commerce Secretary Lutnick stated that Commerce funding of '4% or less' of a project's total value appeared more appropriate than earlier CHIPS award ratios.
evidence_found: "In June 2025, Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick testified to the Senate Committee on Appropriations that some of the contracts made between DOC and awardees of direct funding under the CHIPS Act could be improved. He noted that '4% or less' of funding for a project's total value from DOC appeared 'more appropriate.'" (CRS R49031)
notes: Context: June 2025 Senate Appropriations testimony. The comparison to 'earlier CHIPS award ratios' is implied by the context (existing contracts could be improved), not stated verbatim.

original_interpretation: Samsung's approximately US$4.7 billion CHIPS award equalled 12.8% of its US$37 billion expected investment in Austin and Taylor, Texas.
evidence_found: "Samsung's estimated total investment for the expansion and construction of fabs in Austin, TX, and Taylor, TX, was $37 billion. The approximately $4.7 billion funding award from DOC to support this project constituted 12.8% of the expected investment for this project." (CRS R49031)
notes: Ratio is CRS's calculation from a company-estimated investment figure (4,745/37,000 = 12.8%).

original_interpretation: TSMC and Micron brought their CHIPS awards to under 4% of their total project investment by increasing their capital commitments; CRS found only 2 of the 40 funded projects had direct funding of 5% or less of projected capex.
evidence_found: "Two awardees, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (TSMC) and Micron, brought their awards' share of their total investment to under 4% by increasing their capital commitments." and "According to GAO, 2 of the 40 projects had received direct funding awards from DOC that made up 5% or less of their total projected capital expenditure." (CRS R49031)
correction: The '2 of the 40 projects' finding is GAO's (reported by CRS, citing GAO), not CRS's own finding; the TSMC/Micron under-4% statement is CRS's.

original_interpretation: In January 2026 USA Rare Earth received a nonbinding letter of intent from Commerce proposing US$277 million of CHIPS direct funding and up to US$1.3 billion of collateral-backed loans in return for equity.
evidence_found: "By contrast, in January 2026, USA Rare Earth received a nonbinding letter of intent from the Department of Commerce that proposed to extend funds from the CHIPS Act ($277 million in direct funding and up to $1.3 billion in collateral-backed loan) in return for equity." (CRS R49031); footnote: "USA Rare Earth did not receive the award under the incentives program for commercial fabs."
notes: Not under the commercial fabs incentives program; a nonbinding LOI, not an award.

original_interpretation: A White House fact sheet on the Investment Accelerator order listed negotiating 'better CHIPS Act deals than the previous Administration' as an objective.
evidence_found: "A White House fact sheet on the E.O. included the negotiation of 'better CHIPS Act deals than the previous [Biden] Administration' as one of the objectives of the Investment Accelerator." (CRS R49031, Award Requirements section)
notes: Secondary citation via CRS; the White House fact sheet itself was not re-opened.
